title: Navigating AI’s Frontier in 2025 - Grace Isford, Lux Capital
talk_summary: A VC keynote arguing AI agents fail not from dramatic hallucinations but from small cumulative errors compounding across multi-step tasks, and proposing five mitigations: data curation, evals, scaffolding, UX, and multimodality. Mostly strategic framing, but the error-compounding math and scaffolding/checkpoint ideas are directly copyable.

takeaways.technique: Error-compounding budget: minimize step count and raise per-step accuracy
takeaways.what_they_do: Quantifies how per-step accuracy decays over long chains, arguing multi-agent multi-step systems amplify tiny errors, so reliability work should target step count and per-step correctness rather than end-state retries.
takeaways.evidence_quote: over 50 consecutive steps you actually realize a pretty big disparity here there's actually a 50% difference after 50 tasks
takeaways.numbers: 99% per-step agent drops to ~60% over 50 steps; 95% agent diverges by ~50% relative

takeaways.what_they_do: Wrap agent execution in infrastructure logic so one failure doesn't cascade, and insert checkpoints where the agent verifies state or halts for correction before continuing.
takeaways.evidence_quote: could we add a checkpoint for this AI agent to verify the Trine for traffic or maybe steer it back in the right direction

takeaways.technique: Personal, workflow-specific evals instead of leaderboards
takeaways.what_they_do: Argues verifiable benchmarks don't cover preference-laden tasks; collect human preference signals and build evals tied to the actual user workflow, sometimes just trying it yourself.
takeaways.evidence_quote: Sometimes the best eval is just trying out the agent yourself and Vibes based on your needs with no number or leaderboard

takeaways.technique: Curated feedback flywheel from agent outputs
takeaways.what_they_do: Treat data the agent produces (and corrections to it) as a first-class asset, recycling it back so the system improves over time rather than staying static.
takeaways.evidence_quote: how do you design an agent data flywheel from day one so every time a user uses the product it automatically improves

takeaways.what_they_do: Recommends agents ask clarifying questions up front to confirm the goal before acting, rather than guessing and compounding wrong assumptions.
takeaways.evidence_quote: asking clarifying questions to make sure it fully got the picture of what I'm trying to accomplish
